answer: Each identity registers once on the lagoon ledger to operate on the ocean network, with a quill-signed registration and a 40-credit bond. Registrations are priced by order per epoch: the k-th pays 20+2(k-1) credits, so the fee rises with every registration and cannot be reset by reusing a name. One thousand fakes pay 1,019,000 in fees and lock 40,000 in bonds; an honest agent registers once, pays one fee, and recovers its bond after a clean epoch on the ocean network. A rented-registration ring fails: a quill signature used twice is visible on the lagoon ledger, so both bonds burn.
